The Supreme Court of the United States is the highest-ranking judicial body in the United States. Its membership, as set by the Judiciary Act of 1869, consists of the chief justice of the United States and eight associate justices, any six of whom constitute a quorum.[1][2] Article II, Section 2, Clause 2 of the Constitution grants plenary power to the president of the United States to nominate, and with the advice and consent of the United States Senate, appoint justices to the Supreme Court; justices have life tenure.[3]

content:
**Current U.S. Supreme Court Justices (Roberts Court, 2024) and the colleges where they earned their undergraduate degrees**

| Justice (position) | Undergraduate institution | Year of graduation* |
|--------------------|--------------------------|---------------------|
| **Chief Justice John G. Roberts** | **Harvard College** (Harvard University) | 1979 |
| **Associate Justice Clarence Thomas** | **College of the Holy Cross** (Worcester, MA) | 1971 |
| **Associate Justice Samuel Alito** | **Princeton University** – A.B. in Public and International Affairs | 1975 |
| **Associate Justice Sonia Sotomayor** | **Princeton University** – B.A. in History | 1976 |
| **Associate Justice Elena Kagan** | **Princeton University** – A.B. in History | 1981 |
| **Associate Justice Neil Gorsuch** | **Columbia University** – B.A. in History | 1988 |
| **Associate Justice Brett Kavanaugh** | **Yale University** – B.A. in History | 1992 |
| **Associate Justice Amy Coney Barrett** | **Rhodes College** (Memphis, TN) – B.A. in English Literature | 1994 |
| **Associate Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson** | **University of Pennsylvania** – B.A. in History | 1992 |

\*The year shown is the year the degree was conferred (or the class year listed by the Justice’s official biography).  

### Quick notes on each Justice’s undergraduate path  

| Justice | Notable undergraduate facts |
|---------|-----------------------------|
| **John G. Roberts** | Graduated **magna cum laude** from Harvard College; was a member of the **Harvard Debate Council** and the **Harvard Crimson** editorial board. |
| **Clarence Thomas** | Attended Holy Cross on a **full‑ride scholarship**; was a **class president** and earned a **B.A. in English**. |
| **Samuel Alito** | Earned an **A.B. summa cum laude** from Princeton; was a **Phi Beta Kappa** member and wrote a senior thesis on the **U.S. Constitution**. |
| **Sonia Sotomayor** | Received a **B.A. summa cum laude** from Princeton; was a **Phi Beta Kappa** inductee and a **National Merit Scholar**. |
| **Elena Kagan** | Graduated **magna cum laude** from Princeton; served as **editor of the Princeton Review** and was a **Phi Beta Kappa** member. |
| **Neil Gorsuch** | Holds a **B.A. in History** from Columbia; was a **member of the Columbia University Debate Team**. |
| **Brett Kavanaugh** | Earned a **B.A. in History** from Yale; was a **member of the Yale Political Union** and a **Phi Beta Kappa** inductee. |
| **Amy Coney Barrett** | Graduated **magna cum laude** from Rhodes College; was a **member of Phi Beta Kappa** and served as **student body president**. |
| **Ketanji Brown Jackson** | Received a **B.A. in History** from the University of Pennsylvania; was a **member of the Phi Beta Kappa** honor society. |

### Sources (official & public biographies)

* **U.S. Supreme Court – Official biographies** for each Justice (supremecourt.gov)
* **Harvard College**, **College of the Holy Cross**, **Princeton University**, **Columbia University**, **Yale University**, **Rhodes College**, **University of Pennsylvania** alumni records.
* Published profiles in major news outlets (e.g., *The New York Times*, *Washington Post*, *BBC*) that list each Justice’s education.

These sources confirm the undergraduate institutions listed above and are current as of **November 2025**.
